newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to open television to private business.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to open television to private business.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government will issue an ordinance to open television and radio to multiple private broadcasters, Information Minister Irshad Ahmed Haqqani said on Tuesday.
He told Reuters the aim of the ordinnce, to be announced later on Tuesday or on Wednesday, was to broaden the scope well beyond the currently limited number of television and radio broadcasters.
Haqqani said the only completely privately owned network, Shaheen Pay Television, which also runs FM radio stations in major cities, was expected to challenge the ordinance in court.
"They believe they have exclusive rights for 10 years and will go to the courts," he said.

Shaheen Pay TV was given a licence to broadcast during the rule of ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto. President Farooq Leghari dismissed her government on disputed corruption charges in November, and new elections are scheduled for February 3.
Shaheen is also the only privately-owned radio broadcaster. In television, it competes with state-owned Pakistan Television and the partly government-owned Shalimar Television Network.
Haqqani said the text of the ordinance, approved by the caretaker cabinet on Monday, stated specifically that there would be no private monopolies.
If the courts upheld the government ordinance, Shaheen would have 90 days to apply for a new licence.

Whether Shaheen would be given a new licence, and whether other broadcasters would be given them, would be decided by a seven-member Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (EMRA) headed by a retired Supreme Court judge.
Haqqani said the ordinance would be valid for four months and would have to be approved by the National Assembly, but Leghari could extend it if necessary.
"We're very proud of this," said the former journalist. "It's a healthy and progressive step."
